facts.text: Flushing is a city in Genesee County. It sits within the survey area of Flushing Charter Township but is administered separately from it.
The Flint River flows north along the southern and western portions of the city, and Main Street crosses it on a closed spandrel concrete arch bridge completed in May 1922.
Flushing's Main Street Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1983, covers Main Street from Maple Street to 628 East Main Street.
The historic district's commercial buildings reflect Italianate and early twentieth century styles, and its homes include Greek Revival, Italianate, Queen Anne, Colonial Revival and bungalow styles.
The restored 1888 Flushing Depot at 431 West Main Street is now the Flushing Area Museum and Cultural Center.
Riverview Park, a 7.4 acre city park on the Flint River, has a bandshell, picnic facilities and a playscape, and the Bicentennial Walkway connects it to downtown.
Cornwell Park is a small, landscaped downtown park with benches, set on a former bank site.
The Flushing Riverview Trail is a 1.4 mile non-motorized path that starts at the Main Street Bridge and winds through forest and wetlands along the Flint River.

The annual Flushing Candlewalk, a Flushing Area Chamber of Commerce tradition held over two evenings in early December, lights the streets with thousands of candles, and Santa arrives in a Parade of Lights before the official Christmas tree is lit.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Flushing, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Christmas light installation for Flushing homes: rooflines, porches, tree wraps and shrubs, designed, installed and taken down. Call (248) 756-8915.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Flushing, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Rooflines, porches, trees and shrubs lit in clean, even lines. We design the display, hang it, keep it working through the season and take it down after the holidays.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Flushing's older homes give a lighting design plenty to work with. In the Main Street Historic District you will find Greek Revival, Italianate, Queen Anne, Colonial Revival and bungalow houses, and each one wants its own plan. A Queen Anne's steep, irregular roof can carry layered outlines on every gable. A bungalow's low roof and deep porch often call for the porch framed and the shrubs lit below it. Where a yard has a big shade tree or a row of evergreens, a careful wrap can anchor the whole display. We plan around the house you actually have, then hang it so it reads cleanly from the sidewalk, which matters in a town that walks its own streets for the Candlewalk.
considerations: Italianate brackets, Queen Anne gables and Greek Revival cornices are the reason these houses are worth lighting. We route each strand to follow the lines of the trim without crowding it, so the architecture still shows at night, and our crews take extra care around older paint and wood.

Tall trunks and wide canopies are hard to wrap well from a ladder. Our bucket-truck crews handle the high branches wherever the yard allows truck access, which keeps the spacing even from the base of the trunk to the top of the wrap and keeps you off the ladder entirely.

The Candlewalk brings Flushing out onto its streets over two evenings in early December, which makes it a natural target for having your own house lit. Installs commonly run from October into early December, so sending your request in early fall gives you the widest choice of install dates.
faq: Do you install Christmas lights in Flushing?

Yes. Flushing is part of our Genesee County service area, along with Flint, Burton, Grand Blanc and Davison. Send your address through the estimate form or call (248) 756-8915, and we will set up a time to look at the house and talk through the design you have in mind.
What does the free estimate include?

We look over your roofline, trees, shrubs and outlets, then talk through the look you want. The written estimate that follows spells out what is included, covering design, installation, in-season service and takedown after the holidays, so you can compare options before you commit to anything.
Can you light an older home near the historic district?

Yes. Older houses tend to have more gables, deeper porches and more trim detail than newer builds, which gives the design more to work with. We plan the layout around the architecture. If you need to run the plan past anyone first, the written estimate describes it clearly enough to share.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Flushing, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Holiday lighting for Flushing businesses: Main Street storefronts, offices, condos and HOAs. Building outlines and tree wraps by bucket-truck crews.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Flushing, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Storefront outlines, wrapped trees and entrance lighting for Flushing businesses, offices and associations, installed from the bucket and removed after the season.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Downtown Flushing centers on Main Street. The Main Street Historic District stretches from Maple Street to 628 East Main, lined with Italianate and early twentieth century commercial buildings whose cornices and window rhythms look striking when traced in light. Cornwell Park, a small landscaped park on a former bank site, sits downtown, and the Bicentennial Walkway links Riverview Park on the Flint River to downtown. That makes the season a real opportunity for a storefront. When the Candlewalk fills the streets in early December, a building with clean outlines and a wrapped tree at the entry is the one people remember. We handle it from design through takedown, so your staff never climbs a ladder.
considerations: Italianate storefronts have cornices, window hoods and parapets that look sharp traced in light. We plan runs that follow those lines and work from the bucket truck on the upper stories, so every outline stays straight and the building still reads as itself after dark.

A downtown storefront has customers coming and going during install season. We agree on staging, truck placement and timing with you ahead of time, so the work fits around your business hours and the entrance stays clear for the people you want walking through it.

Not every commercial property in Flushing sits downtown. Offices, multi-tenant buildings, condo communities and subdivision entrances can all carry a coordinated display. One plan and one point of contact cover design, installation, in-season service and takedown for the whole property.
faq: Do you light businesses in downtown Flushing?

Yes. Flushing is within our service area, and storefronts, restaurants, offices and other businesses are a core part of our work. We can light a single facade or plan a matching look across several neighboring buildings. Start with the estimate form or call (248) 756-8915.
When should a Flushing business book?

Early fall is ideal. The commercial install season generally stretches from October into early December, and a business that wants its display glowing before the Candlewalk will have more date options by booking ahead. Takedown is scheduled after the holidays, once the season has wrapped up.
Can you work with a property manager or association board?

Yes. Property managers, HOAs and condo boards are among the customers we serve. We can walk the site with whoever makes the decision and send a written estimate that spells out what is included, which makes it easier to take to an owner or a board for approval.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Christmas Lights in Flushing, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent Christmas lights for Flushing homes. App-controlled colors and schedules for Christmas, game days and everyday accent light. Free estimates.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: One install, and your roofline is ready for every holiday after it. Choose colors and schedules from an app, for Christmas, game days or a quiet everyday glow.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Permanent lighting suits a house you plan to enjoy for years. The lights mount along the roofline once and stay there, and you run them from an app: warm white through the Christmas season, bold colors for game days, a soft outline on an ordinary weeknight. In a city where homes range from Greek Revival to bungalow, the layout has to fit the house. A bungalow's long, low eaves take a simple continuous outline well. A Colonial Revival front, even and symmetrical, looks crisp with a single clean line. A Queen Anne's many angles take more planning, and we map every corner before anything goes up. Then we install it and show you how the app works.
considerations: Fitting the style of the house

Flushing's older styles each suggest a different outline. Symmetrical Colonial Revival fronts favor one steady line, while Queen Anne rooflines ask which gables to feature and which to leave dark. We make those choices with you during the estimate, so the result looks intentional.

Think about how many nights you would use it. A December display is what seasonal installation is built for. If you would also light the house for Halloween, the Fourth of July, a graduation party or a dark winter evening, permanent lighting starts to make more sense.

Where power is available shapes the whole plan. We look at outlet locations and at how the runs turn each corner of the roof, then lay out the lights so they read as one clean outline at night and look tidy along the eaves by day.
faq: Is permanent lighting available in Flushing?

Yes. We design and install permanent roofline lighting for homes throughout our Genesee County service area, Flushing included. It starts with a free estimate, where we look at your roofline and power and talk through how often and for what occasions you would use the lights.
Will it work on an older home?

In most cases, yes. Older homes often have more corners, gables and trim detail, so the layout takes more planning. We look closely at the roof and eaves during the estimate and give you an honest view of what will look good and what is better left unlit.
What can I do with the app?

Change colors, pick scenes and set schedules. Common uses include warm white for the holidays, team colors on game days, colors for birthdays and a soft outline as everyday accent lighting. We set it up with you and walk you through the controls before we leave.
